# Chip Integrity

> An open, MIT-licensed tester for silent computation errors in AI chips. It runs a compute probe (matrix multiplies at three shapes and four precisions plus exact FP8, every output element checked against a float64 reference with Higham's rounding bound, widened for tensor-core truncation at fp16 and bf16, and against run 0 bit for bit) a kernel probe (softmax, layer norm, GELU, rotary embeddings and fused attention, checked the same two ways against derived bounds) a checksum-protected matrix multiply (Huang and Abraham ABFT, with thresholds derived from the same arithmetic model and the rectangle blind spot measured), a data pattern probe (wide exponents, full mantissas, cancellation, alternating signs, sparsity, subnormals with flush detection, near-overflow and int8 extremes, through the matrix multiply) a soak probe (one fixed matrix multiply run back to back for hours, every result compared bit for bit with a verified first result, with temperature, clocks, power and the driver's clock-event reasons recorded per one-minute window), an error counter cross-check around every run (NVIDIA ECC counts, remapped rows and retired pages before and after, with a verdict on whether the hardware noticed what the probe found), and a memory probe (six patterns written into every 32-bit word of device memory and read back exactly). Results are written in the Open Compute Project Test and Validation format, and every published row links to its result file. Maintained by Yasha Khandelwal, Bengaluru, India.

Site: https://chipintegrity.org/
Code: https://github.com/tech4biz-yasha/ai-chip-integrity (MIT)
Install: pip install ai-chip-integrity (Python 3.10 or newer), then chip-integrity run (every probe and its self-test, ten OCP result files) and chip-integrity soak --minutes N (hours under load, one more file). Docker: ghcr.io/tech4biz-yasha/ai-chip-integrity
Cite: Yasha Khandelwal, ai-chip-integrity, version 0.4.3, 2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23505677
Contact: yasha.khandelwal@tech4biz.io

## What it measures

Compute probe (screen.py): C = A @ B, 50 runs per shape and precision. Shapes 1024x1024x1024, 4096x4096x4096 and 32x4096x11008. Precisions fp32, fp16, bf16 and int8, plus FP8 (E4M3) with full and fast accumulation where the device supports it. Verdicts: no-silent-errors, silent-data-corruption, outside-error-bound, nondeterministic-kernel.

Memory probe (memcheck.py): fills most of the device memory, writes all zeros, all ones, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, an address hash and its inverse into every word, waits 2 seconds, reads back and compares exactly. Verdicts: no-memory-errors, memory-errors, with byte offsets and bad-bit masks logged.

Kernel probe (kernels.py): softmax, layer norm, GELU (erf form), rotary position embeddings (sin and cos of FP32 angles up to 4095 rad) and scaled dot product attention through the device's own kernels, 25 runs per kernel and precision, fp32, fp16 and bf16. Bounds derived by rounding-error analysis under one written arithmetic model (arith.py): FP32 rounds to nearest, tensor cores accumulate faithfully in FP32 with truncation allowed, exp, divide and square roots stay within eight ulps, and erf, sin and cos within 2^-20 absolute. The model id is recorded in every result file. Same verdicts as the compute probe.

Self-test: every row is paired with an injection run that plants faults and must catch all of them. From v0.4.2 the faults alternate between single random bit flips and faults shaped like NVIDIA's gate-level measurements (Tung et al., DSN 2026, arXiv:2605.04213): warp-aligned groups of zeroed, multi-bit-flipped or NaN/infinity values.

## Measured so far

One page per chip, generated from the result files. Silent faults are runs that differed from their own repeat, checksums that did not agree, memory words that came back wrong or results under load that differed from the verified first one; results outside the proven bound agreed with every repeat but sat outside the bound, which is a faulty unit or a software stack outside the arithmetic model:
- AMD Radeon Pro 5500M (MPS) x86_64: https://chipintegrity.org/chips/amd-radeon-pro-5500m-mps-x86-64.html (last tested 2026-10-21; 1,190 compute runs, 0 silent faults, 140 results outside the proven bound, 186 of 186 planted faults caught)
- Apple GPU (MPS) arm64: https://chipintegrity.org/chips/apple-gpu-mps-arm64.html (last tested 2026-10-10; 1,785 compute runs, 0 silent faults, 0 results outside the proven bound, 264 of 264 planted faults caught)
- NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB: https://chipintegrity.org/chips/nvidia-a100-sxm4-80gb.html (last tested 2026-10-07; 600 compute runs, 0 silent faults, 0 results outside the proven bound, 90 of 90 planted faults caught)
- NVIDIA B200: https://chipintegrity.org/chips/nvidia-b200.html (last tested 2026-10-19; 2,515 compute runs, 0 silent faults, 0 results outside the proven bound, 351 of 351 planted faults caught)
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090: https://chipintegrity.org/chips/nvidia-geforce-rtx-4090.html (last tested 2026-10-11; 2,515 compute runs, 0 silent faults, 0 results outside the proven bound, 351 of 351 planted faults caught)
- NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3: https://chipintegrity.org/chips/nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3.html (last tested 2026-10-10; 2,515 compute runs, 0 silent faults, 0 results outside the proven bound, 351 of 351 planted faults caught)
- NVIDIA H200: https://chipintegrity.org/chips/nvidia-h200.html (last tested 2026-10-08; 600 compute runs, 0 silent faults, 0 results outside the proven bound, 90 of 90 planted faults caught)
- NVIDIA RTX A5000: https://chipintegrity.org/chips/nvidia-rtx-a5000.html (last tested 2026-10-11; 2,055 compute runs, 0 silent faults, 0 results outside the proven bound, 297 of 297 planted faults caught)

## Findings

What measuring real chips has turned up, each with its evidence:
- 2026-10-21, Metal through PyTorch 2.2.2 sits outside the arithmetic model: https://chipintegrity.org/findings/metal-pytorch-2-2-2.html. On an AMD Radeon Pro 5500M, the backend's sin and cos measured 1.22e-4 against the model's 9.5e-7 allowance, and four more fp16 steps sat outside their bound while every run agreed with every other.
- 2026-10-15, NVIDIA's own fault patterns, caught on a real GPU: https://chipintegrity.org/findings/nvidia-fault-patterns.html. The self-test now plants faults shaped like NVIDIA's gate-level measurements. On an RTX 4090 the reference check alone flagged all 294.
- 2026-10-11, When ECC is off, the memory error counters cannot see anything: https://chipintegrity.org/findings/ecc-off.html. Two rented cards ran with ECC switched off, so their counters could not move. The tester now says so instead of calling them quiet.
- 2026-10-10, BF16 matrix multiplies on Intel AMX treat tiny inputs as zero: https://chipintegrity.org/findings/intel-amx-bf16.html. Above 16 × 16 × 16, BF16 matrix multiplies on AMX CPUs treat subnormal inputs as zero, whatever set_flush_denormal says.
